Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Key pain & goals we heard:
- Primary product: real-time triage assistant embedded in clinician EHR workflows; median latency needs to be low to avoid workflow disruption.
- Pain: current prototype using hosted APIs has inconsistent p95 latency and unpredictable cost under burst.
- Goal: target P95 end-to-end response latency <= 250ms for typical 80–150 token answers, sustained 120 qps with 2:1 burst headroom, and consistent unit cost within procurement thresholds.

Technical summary (what we committed to surface):
- Model candidates: 7B/8B open variants for initial trial; quantized int4 profiles for Dedicated to meet cost/SLO tradeoffs.
- Topology: Hybrid approach — Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with Smart Routing to fallback to hosted variants during capacity constraints.
- Caching: prefix + KV cache for repeated prompts (expected 30–40% hit rate on typical triage prompts).
- Canary & rollouts: canary at 2% traffic, ramp to 25% then 100% with rollback on quality regressions flagged by your eval set.

Action items (proposed):
1) Redwood to send a one-page SLO matrix and a draft topology sketch (will attach).
2) Medlinea to share a 1-week sample of 95/latency histograms or synthetic qps profile and 10 representative prompts for quality gating.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Kar tik (runtime) and Monica (ops) — suggest Wed 6/9 or Thu 6/10.

Please reply with which deep-dive slot works and confirm the data we should expect from your side. I attached a quick SLO template we will fill after the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

—

Elena + Rajesh — thanks for the follow-up and the data you said you'd share. A few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so the session is focused.

1) Baseline performance assumptions (internal):
- Candidate model: redwood/gpt-8b-qat-int4 or redwood/gpt-7b-int8 as fallback. For 256-token contexts we estimate per-request generation latency of ~110–160ms on Dedicated H100s with batching disabled (single-request low-latency path). On A100s expect ~150–220ms.
- Throughput: a single H100 in a Dedicated pool can sustain ~250–300 concurrent small requests / second with autoscaling (depends on request size and batching policy). For steady 120 qps we recommend a 2-node Dedicated pool with headroom for 2x burst.

2) SLO shaping & measurement:
- We'll define P50/P90/P95 for both model-only and end-to-end. Redwood will expose token-level breakdowns in the Console (compiler+kernel time, KV cache lookup, network/ingress).
- KV cache expectations: with the triage prompts you described, realistic hit rates of 25–35% reduce model time by ~30% on hits; we'll run a small experiment to validate.

3) Topology & fallback strategy:
- Primary: Dedicated us-west pool (H100s) with autoscale and reserved capacity.
- Fallback: Hosted redwood endpoint running smaller quantized variants in eu-west/us-east as configured. Smart routing policy: prefer Dedicated until latency or capacity breach, then gracefully route a percentage of traffic to hosted variant with model-version mapping to preserve semantics.
- Canary plan: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48–72 hours, with automatic rollback on quality/regression thresholds tied to your prompt eval set.

4) Cost delta rough numbers (very approximate, ballpark):
- Int8 8B on Dedicated H100: baseline unit cost X (we'll provide a calc) — roughly 1.0x baseline.
- Int4 8B on Dedicated H100: ~0.6–0.7x baseline (fewer GPU cycles, smaller memory footprint); tradeoff: slightly higher quantization risk on some prompt patterns.
- Quantization savings are model- and prompt-dependent; we'll run a quick eval on your sample prompts and include token-level cost estimates in the SLO matrix.

Attachments: I attached an initial topology sketch and a blank SLO matrix Mark us shared. Please confirm if we should include a compliance (SOC2) artifact in the next send; procurement will ask.

Looking forward to Thu 6/10 10:00am PT.

—
Karthik Iyer
